translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Woolf’s long chained sentences, unsignalled shifts between minds and repeated refrains are kept, without splitting into short sentences or adding connectives.
decisions.rationale: The novel’s effect is carried in the flow and the passage between consciousnesses.

decisions.decision: The old woman’s sound-song (‘ee um fah um so …’) is kept as in the source and not translated.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Heaven knows if she didn’t think him the most original mind’ was rendered with inverted polarity; corrected.
Milly Brush, a girl, was addressed as ‘bà’; now ‘cô’.
‘Feasts on’ (of Conversion feeding on a will) was rendered as celebrating; now ‘ngốn lấy ý chí’.
Miss Kilman was called ‘bà cô’ (spinster aunt), a mis-register; now ‘cô ấy’ / ‘cô Kilman’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: The title is translated and the Dalloway name is kept.

glossary.source_term: narration of Clarissa / Peter / Septimus / Rezia / Elizabeth / Miss Kilman
glossary.draft_rendering: Clarissa (bà only where a pronoun is needed); Peter (ông); Septimus (anh); Rezia (cô); Elizabeth (cô bé); cô Kilman
glossary.rationale: One reference system through the stream of consciousness.
A recurring Big Ben motif is kept constant.

glossary.source_term: Fear no more the heat o’ the sun
glossary.draft_rendering: Đừng sợ nữa cái nóng của mặt trời / Cũng đừng sợ cơn thịnh nộ dữ dội của mùa đông.
glossary.rationale: The Cymbeline refrain is kept as a two-line verse unit.

glossary.draft_rendering: Là Clarissa, ông nói. / Vì bà đây rồi.
glossary.rationale: The last two units close the novel.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #71865, an electronic transcription of Mrs. Dalloway by Virginia Woolf (1925). The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated with the first edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: An ambiguous ‘she’ is fixed to Elizabeth in unit 24; the English leaves it open for a moment.
Calque in unit 3 left as is.
‘Robes’ is rendered ‘áo dài’, a Vietnamese garment, in unit 306.

title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Bà Dalloway’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: ‘Mrs. Dalloway said she would buy the flowers herself.’
The last unit: ‘For there she was.’
